comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part that surprised me: German, French and Italian are all state languages across a Swiss border, so three quarters of Switzerland's linguistic identity is shared with its neighbours. Romansh is not. About forty thousand speakers in Grisons, national since 1938, official since 1996, and recognised officially in no other country on Earth. Sources are listed in the description if you want to dig. Is there a language in your region that stops dead at the border, and does the state there give it any official standing?
